changes.summary: For the Paris Opera House, Charles Garnier wanted decoration in perfect harmony with its architecture. He called on artists from the Paris Beaux-Arts and Villa Medici, who rose to the occasion by drawing inspiration from the Italian master Raphael. As its designer, Charles Garnier was closely involved in the drafting of an interior decoration program for the Opera House that would be in symbiosis with his architectural project. He entrusted its creation to the Beaux-Arts’ and Villa Medici’s fellow students, Jules Delaunay, Charles Baudry and Félix Barrias. The delicacy of their black chalk sketches and studies bequeathed to the national collections, as well as the preparation of the paper they used, evidences an admiring debt of gratitude to the great master who decorated the Palazzo Farnese and the Vatican.
